page: Amazon Web Services i7i.metal-48xl is a bare-metal storage-optimized server configured on the x86_64 architecture. It features dual Intel Xeon 8559C processors delivering 96 physical cores and 192 dedicated hardware threads clocked at 3.2 GHz, backed by 320 MB of L3 cache. The platform is provisioned with 1,536 GB of DDR5 system memory operating at 6 GHz, yielding an 8 GB per core ratio. Local high-speed storage is integrated directly via 45,000 GB of NVMe SSDs, supported by 100 Gbps of baseline networking bandwidth without hypervisor intervention.

Benchmark results place the multi-core processing and storage capabilities in the top tier. The instance scored 171,453.48 in multi-core stress-ng tests and 134,309.48 in PassMark CPU tests. The memory subsystem recorded 576.98 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth and 237.8 GB/sec write bandwidth on large 256 MB blocks. Hardware support for Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 accelerates vectorized compute, delivering top-tier performance in database operations (37,094.84 in PassMark) and 223.07 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. Single-core throughput is moderate to high, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2,314.0.

The bare-metal architecture bundles high-density NVMe storage with massive DDR5 memory on a single dedicated node, providing high resource consolidation that reduces multi-instance management overhead and bypasses virtualization penalties. While single-thread efficiency is standard for dense multi-socket Intel architectures, the sheer hardware density and 100 Gbps network pipe provide substantial bandwidth for demanding data pipelines.

The AWS i7i.metal-48xl is structured for high-capacity transactional databases, distributed in-memory data stores like Redis, real-time analytics, large-scale Clang compilation jobs, and high-throughput data warehousing requiring low-latency NVMe access.
